The general shape, worth carrying:\n\n> **A guard changes what gets measured, and every summary computed downstream of it silently\n> changes meaning.**\n\nA dirty-tree guard correctly declined to measure three repos; the denominator moved 18→15; seven\nvaccines appeared to improve and none had. **A wrong denominator is worse than a wrong finding,\nbecause it gets quoted rather than checked.**\n\n---\n\n## Standing facts about this estate\n\n- The **canonical repos** are under `OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/`. Directories in the home folder\n  are **worktrees** — their `.git` is a file pointing back. Enumerate repos from the GitHub API,\n  never from disk: one session scanned 15 when the account had 30, and 33 by morning.\n- **No `gh` CLI, no token.** GitHub API is unauthenticated: **60 req/hour, per IP, shared by every\n  agent and the estate's own workflows.** It was exhausted once and a gate degraded as a result.\n  Query the free `/rate_limit` first; do not sample below 25 remaining. `git fetch`/`push` cost\n  nothing. `/actions/runs/<id>/logs` returns 403 — reproduce failures locally instead, which is\n  better evidence than a log anyway.\n- `python3` is a broken Windows Store stub. Use `python`.\n- 20 cores. `--shared` clones are instant. A full estate scan is under a minute. Multiprocessing\n  workers must live in a real `.py` file with a `__main__` guard — heredoc-piped code crashes the\n  pool on Windows.\n- `Counter[400]` and `Counter[400.0]` are the **same key** in Python. This produced a false defect\n  report once.\n- `require()` picks its parser by extension: it reads a `.lock` as JavaScript and throws. Use\n  `JSON.parse(readFileSync(...))`.\n- A `git clone` of gridatlas on Windows needs `-c core.longpaths=true`, and **even then 12 files\n  under `nightly/…/runs/` are silently absent** while git reports success.\n- Stamps come from `date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M` **evaluated in the same command as the commit**. Reading\n  BST off `git log` put five commits 29–50 minutes ahead; `monotonic-utc-generations` catches it.\n\n## Editing globalgrid2050/index.html\n\n1. `homepage_versions/README.md` requires a numbered snapshot with recorded line/word/char counts\n   and a plain-English change intention **before** any edit. **Fetch before enumerating** — a\n   session overwrote a real snapshot because it listed the folder before fast-forwarding.\n2. `scripts/catalogue_gridatlas_v9.py` fails closed unless the V8 sentinel appears once byte for\n   byte with four leading spaces, and its route appears once. The `GRIDATLAS_V9_AUTOMATION_START/END`\n   markers must survive verbatim.\n3. **The compiler cannot refresh the current-composition row.** `compile_root()` requires the\n   catalogue URL to occur at most once and, when present, the whole entry line to match byte for\n   byte. An `os-strip` banner added on 30 August carries the same href, so the compiler has been\n   unable to run on that file since. That is why the version stamp drifted nine releases.\n\nVerify before every commit: sentinel once, route once, both markers intact, every pre-existing\n`name:` and `note:` string byte-identical, and `AREAS` re-evaluated with node so it still parses.\n\nShip live by default — stamp, commit, push, then poll the live URL and report the SHA-256 match.\n\n## Standing discipline in this estate\n\n- **Never amend a shipped generation.** New fault, new step, new version.\n- **Report measurements, never grade them.**\n- **A skip is not a pass.** A verdict may only say PASS when every check it names actually ran.\n- **Never weaken a shared check to make your lane pass.** Make it more precise and say why.\n- **Redact the payload, not the view.**\n- **Measure the artefact, never the workspace.**\n\n## Working alongside other agents\n\nSeveral lanes run at once — Claude, Codex, Gemini, and subagents of each.\n\n- **Never `git add -A` or `git add .` in this repo.** Stage by explicit path. A commit race here\n  swept another session's in-progress files into an unrelated commit.\n- Fetch immediately before every write, not once per phase. `atlas/current.json` and\n  `index.html` are single files every generation must touch; git cannot merge them meaningfully.\n- If a repo is mid-write by another lane, note it and move on. **Never treat a dirty tree as a\n  defect.**\n- If another lane already shipped a fix you were about to make, log it as covered and move on.\n\n## How to add a session\n\nCreate `sessions/<YYYYMMDDHHMM>-<slug>/`. Do not rewrite an earlier session; a correction is a new\nentry that names what it corrects. **Record what you got wrong** — most errors here were caught by\nmeasuring again rather than by reasoning harder, and that is the transferable lesson.\n"
}

`CLAUDE.md` rewritten and pushed as `30fd8c8`. The measurement rule now leads the file, before any estate fact.

## The distillation

Four agents produced **twenty-plus corrections between them tonight**, and almost every one was the same mistake wearing a different face:

> **A measurement that does not name the commit, the branch, and the bytes it read is not a measurement.**

```
dirty tree      working copy mid-edit    → "CI went red on v9.82"   it had not
dirty bytes ×2  CRLF working copy        → invented a checksum failure
                                            AND concealed a real one
wrong branch    Codex's first CI run     → "gridatlas is red"       main was green
```

Its other half, three times in ninety minutes: **a green light that measured nothing.** A proof on the left of `&&` under `set -e`. A guarded check that skipped silently when its input was absent — so **675 of 735 checks had never run on a runner**, and the transformer fix had only ever been verified on a laptop where the repos happened to be neighbours. Two constants in one step, where fixing the second couldn't turn the first green.

And the second-order one, which cost the most to see: **a correction can create its own defect**, because a guard changes what gets measured and every summary downstream of it silently changes meaning. A wrong denominator is worse than a wrong finding — it gets quoted rather than checked.

## Why that's the deliverable, not the code

Eight session directories now, but a session with no memory reads `CLAUDE.md` first. Every rule in it was paid for tonight in a wrong answer, and each one is written so the next session doesn't have to buy it again — including the two that caught *me*: the `&&` proof, and accepting a root cause without running the five lines above it.

## Standing, 03:20Z

The single sentence that explains both halves of D6: **the gridatlas migration split one directory into two roles that used to coincide.** The app moved to `/gridatlas/atlas/`; the release artefacts moved to `/gridatlas/atlas/releases/&lt;release_id&gt;/`. Before, they were one URL. data-gridatlas's watchdog was fetching a manifest from the old combined path — fixed at `8bf88da`. `companies` is linking to the app at the old combined path — still open.

The finding that makes it worth a handoff rather than a one-line edit: **the workflow that would refresh the stale contract is stale in the same way.** It correctly *derives* `live_url` from `live-set.json` at line 82, then asserts the retired shape against that derived value at line 96, so a dispatch dies before writing anything. And line 101 fetches the manifest from the app base, where it 404s, while line 105 fetches the deep link from the app base, where it correctly 200s. Those two lines disagree for a principled reason: a deep link is a property of the app, a manifest is a property of the release, and nothing written before the migration can tell them apart because they were the same URL.

Waiting for the pass-8 window at ~03:47Z. The 90-second poll on `data-grid-gb origin/main` stays armed — still `1c9909d`.</result>

command:

set +e
G=/c/Users/vikra/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub
echo "=== classifying every hit: FROZEN (correct to hold it) vs LIVE (operative) ==="
echo
for d in $G/*/; do
  r=$(basename "$d"); [ -d "$d/.git" ] || continue
  cd "$d" 2>/dev/null || continue
  REF=$(git rev-parse --verify -q origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo origin/main || echo HEAD)
  FILES=$(git grep -I -l -E "gridatlas/[0-9]{12}-atlas-v9/" "$REF" 2>/dev/null | sed "s#^$REF:##")
  [ -z "$FILES" ] && continue
  FROZEN=0; LIVE=0; LIVELIST=""
  for f in $FILES; do
    case "$f" in
      homepage_versions/*|*/workflow-archive/*|sessions/*|*/transcript/*|releases/2026*|archive/*|*-study/*|docs/*|*.md)
        FROZEN=$((FROZEN+1)) ;;
      *)
        LIVE=$((LIVE+1)); LIVELIST="$LIVELIST $f" ;;
    esac
  done
  printf "  %-18s frozen %-4s live %-3s\n" "$r" "$FROZEN" "$LIVE"
  for f in $LIVELIST; do echo "      LIVE  $f"; done
done

**TOOL CALL** — `Bash`  (id `toolu_01VoQwhFYehPrsDSTXJ5JgrV`)

command:

```
set +e
cd /c/Users/vikra/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/globalgrid2050
echo "=== corrected classification, globalgrid2050 ==="
REF=origin/main
TOT=$(git grep -I -l -E "gridatlas/[0-9]{12}-atlas-v9/" $REF | wc -l)
FROZ=$(git grep -I -l -E "gridatlas/[0-9]{12}-atlas-v9/" $REF | grep -cE "homepage_versions/|pipelinenews_intelligence/")
echo "  total $TOT   frozen (snapshots + published releases) $FROZ   live $((TOT-FROZ))"
git grep -I -l -E "gridatlas/[0-9]{12}-atlas-v9/" $REF | grep -vE "homepage_versions/|pipelinenews_intelligence/" | sed "s#^$REF:##" | sed 's/^/    LIVE  /'

echo; echo "=== the homepage's own catalogue rows: which URLs are dead? ==="
python - <<'PY'
import subprocess,re,urllib.request
html=subprocess.run(['git','show','origin/main:index.html'],capture_output=True,text=True,encoding='utf-8').stdout
rows=re.findall(r'\{ name:"([^"]*)", url:"(https://ventusltd\.github\.io/gridatlas/[^"]*)"', html)
seen=set()
for name,url in rows:
    if url in seen: continue
    seen.add(url)
    try:
        req=urllib.request.Request(url, method='HEAD')
        code=urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20).status
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: code=e.code
    except Exception as e: code=str(e)[:22]
    flag='  <-- DEAD' if code!=200 else ''
    print('  %-3s %-58s %s%s' % (code, name[:58], url[:60], flag))
PY
```

## Version 022

Version: \`homepage_v022.html\`

Folder file count after this snapshot:

MD

202609030340: the one dead Grid Atlas link on the public directory

The row "UK Grid Atlas V9 - 202608291239" pointed at
/gridatlas/202608291239-atlas-v9/, which answers 404. It now points at
/gridatlas/atlas/releases/202608291239-atlas-v9/, which answers 200.

The cause, in one sentence, and it explains more than this row: GridAtlas split
one directory into two roles that used to coincide. The served app moved to
/gridatlas/atlas/ and the release artefacts to /gridatlas/atlas/releases/<id>/.
Before the migration they were the same URL, so nothing written earlier can tell
a deep link from a manifest - which is why data-gridatlas's watchdog was
fetching a manifest from the app base and companies is still linking to the app
at the artefact base. This row names an artefact, so it takes the artefact base.

Only the URL changes. Every name: and note: string is byte-identical, verified
by diff; the V8 sentinel, its route and both GRIDATLAS_V9_AUTOMATION markers are
untouched; AREAS re-evaluated with node. homepage_v022.html is the restore point.

Scope, measured rather than assumed. 338 references to the pre-migration shape
exist estate-wide, and reporting that number as a defect count would be wrong:
122 of the 125 in this repository are frozen by design - homepage snapshots and
published immutable releases, correct to hold the URL that was live when they
were cut. I classified them badly on the first pass and counted 103 published
releases as operative, which is the same error the spider has now corrected four
times: counting text about code as code. Three are operative here. This row is
one; the two under state/ describe the app rather than an artefact and are left
for the architect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015VermKtYmhK6PNKrZ7YFnk
MSG
git log --oneline -1 | sed 's/^/  /'
git push -q origin main && echo "  pushed $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"

LH=$(sha256sum index.html | cut -d' ' -f1)
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  [ "$(curl -s https://globalgrid2050.com/ | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$LH" ] && { echo "  HOMEPAGE MATCH $LH"; break; }
  sleep 15
done
echo "  --- both catalogue links, live ---"
for u in "https://ventusltd.github.io/gridatlas/atlas/" "https://ventusltd.github.io/gridatlas/atlas/releases/202608291239-atlas-v9/"; do

Withdrawing D14 entirely. The gridatlas attestation was never stale. I reported it to you as a confirmed finding, then reported again that it had been falsely silenced, and both messages were wrong.

live-set.json was written at 8fb95a2, the same commit that set the pointer generation. 1762170 and cc449d5 were tooling changes that cut no new composition, so the pointer correctly did not advance and the attestation correctly did not need refreshing. The state was right the whole time.

attestation-freshness fired because at 8fb95a2 the newest commit subject matching /live|verif|accept/ happened to fall after the newest matching /scope|cartridge|compos|promote/. It never opened either file.

Name a release from its release_id, not from the cartridge it added.\");\n      }\n    }\n    return out;\n  };\n\n=== page-data-block-parses: what it reports ===\n        }\n        if (c === '\"' || c === \"'\" || c === \"`\") { quote = c; stripped.push(\" \"); continue; }\n        stripped.push(c);\n        if (c === \"[\" || c === \"{\") depth++;\n        else if (c === \"]\" || c === \"}\") { depth--; if (depth === 0) { end = i; break; } }\n      }\n      if (quote) { findings.push(`${name}: a string literal is never closed; the block cannot parse`); continue; }\n      if (end === -1) { findings.push(`${name}: brackets never balance; the block cannot parse`); continue; }\n      // Outside strings, a data literal of objects may only contain structure,\n      // key names and numbers. cd "/c/Users/vikra/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-vikra/5b94bee7-197b-4cfd-944b-d4cf3aa02d18/scratchpad/cvaa-origin"
W="$(pwd)"
echo "=== all five steps, each rc captured on its own line ==="
test "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository)" = false && test "$(git rev-list --count HEAD)" -gt 1
echo "  1 history complete                        rc=$?"
files=$(find vaccines -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
lock=$(node -e "console.log(Object.keys(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('vaccines.lock','utf8'))).length)")
test "$files" -eq "$lock"
echo "  2 files($files) == lock($lock)                    rc=$?"
node tools/selftest.mjs > "$W/st.log" 2>&1
echo "  3 antibodies fire/silent                  rc=$?"
test "$(tail -n 1 "$W/st.log")" = 'all antibodies fire on disease and stay silent on health'
echo "  3b last line exact                        rc=$?"
node inoculate.mjs . --no-write > "$W/in.log" 2>/dev/null
echo "  4 registry immune                         rc=$?"
test "$(tail -n 1 "$W/in.log")" = 'repo is immune to all vaccines on file'
echo "  4b last line exact                        rc=$?"
node inoculate.mjs . --no-write --json > "$W/run.jsonl" 2>/dev/null
node -e "
const fs=require('fs');
const lines=fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1],'utf8').split('\n').filter(l=>l.startsWith('{\"schema\":\"cvaa.run.v1\"'));
if(lines.length!==1) throw new Error('expected one record, got '+lines.length);
const run=JSON.parse(lines[0]);
if(run.status!=='immune') throw new Error('status '+run.status);
if(run.shallow!==false||run.context?.commit_count<2) throw new Error('history incomplete');
const active=fs.readdirSync('vaccines').filter(f=>f.endsWith('.md')).filter(f=>!/^superseded_by:/m.test(fs.readFileSync('vaccines/'+f,'utf8'))).length;
if(run.results.length!==active) throw new Error('expected '+active+' got '+run.results.length);
console.log('    active='+active+' results='+run.results.length+' status='+run.status);
" "$W/run.jsonl"
echo "  5 json record agrees                      rc=$?"
rm -f "$W/st.log" "$W/in.log" "$W/run.jsonl"
```

*uuid=`59915160-d9e0-4ce8-bdb4-97aed933e346` · parent=`afd929a3-b70a-4b62-ac8d-92dd4790ab00` · model=`claude-opus-5` · branch=`HEAD`*

**TOOL CALL** — `Bash`  (id `toolu_01D5BEGKzc6ZxJXtoppzQVbc`)

command:

```
set -e
cd "/c/Users/vikra/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-vikra/5b94bee7-197b-4cfd-944b-d4cf3aa02d18/scratchpad/cvaa-origin"
STAMP=$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M)
git add tools/selftest.mjs
git -c user.name="Claude" -c user.email="noreply@anthropic.com" commit -q -F - -- tools/selftest.mjs <<MSG
${STAMP}: the two vaccines added on 31 August get the fixtures they never had

Root cause of a red that has stood since 31 August, and it explains all three
symptoms at once. Two vaccines were added that day - release-name-convention at
15:59Z and page-data-block-parses at 21:46Z - and nothing else about them was
updated. The self-test asserted 23 active results and there were 25. The step
asserted 24 vaccine files and there were 26. And selftest.mjs requires every
antibody to fire on a diseased fixture and stay silent on a clean one, and
neither vaccine had a fixture:

    selftest fixture missing for release-name-convention
    selftest fixture missing for page-data-block-parses
    2 antibody problem(s)

My two earlier commits fixed the two counts. Neither could turn the runner
green, because this is the step that fails, and I could not see which step it
was until the previous commit split one nine-command block into five named
ones. That split earned its keep immediately: the jobs API named
"Antibodies fire on disease and stay silent on health" with no log access.

The fixtures. release-name-convention gets a catalogue where two siblings set
the <Product> em-dash <generation> convention and a third trails its generation
behind invented words - the shape the vaccine was written from, where
"Project Intelligence" was the cartridge a build added rather than the name of
the application. page-data-block-parses gets a data block whose string literal
is never closed, so the array cannot bind and the menu renders empty.

Also fixed here because the self-test could not otherwise run on a developer
machine at all: `new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname` yields /C:/Users/...
on Windows and joins to C:\\C:\\Users\\... inoculate.mjs already resolves this
correctly with fileURLToPath and carries a comment about exactly this; the
self-test did not get the same care. Same fix, same import.

Proven by running all five steps with each exit code captured separately:
history complete, 26 files == 26 lock entries, all antibodies fire and stay
silent, registry immune, and the JSON record agreeing at 25 active results.
Not by reading an echo after an && , which is how I shipped a broken fix twice
tonight.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015VermKtYmhK6PNKrZ7YFnk
MSG
git log --oneline -1 | sed 's/^/  /'
git push -q gh HEAD:main
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
echo "  pushed ${SHA:0:7}  stamp $STAMP  actual $(date -u +%H:%MZ)"

echo; echo "=== the runner's verdict ==="
for i in $(seq 1 16); do
  R=$(curl -s "https://api.github.com/repos/Ventusltd/cvaa/actions/runs?head_sha=$SHA&per_page=5" | python -c "
import sys,json
try:
  rs=[r for r in json.load(sys.stdin).get('workflow_runs',[]) if 'Self-test' in r['name']]
  print('%s %s %s'%(rs[0]['id'],rs[0]['status'],rs[0]['conclusion']) if rs else 'none none none')
except Exception: print('none none none')")
  set -- $R
  echo "  $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) run=$1 status=$2 conclusion=$3"
  [ "$2" = "completed" ] && break
  sleep 25
done
```

**cvaa is green.** Run `33711487895`, conclusion `success` — first pass since 31 August.

```
03:29:48Z  run=33711487895  status=completed  conclusion=success
```

## The root cause, and it explains all three symptoms at once

Two vaccines landed on 31 August — `release-name-convention` at 15:59Z and `page-data-block-parses` at 21:46Z — and **nothing else about them was updated**. That single omission produced three separate failures:

```
self-test asserted 23 active results   there were 25
step asserted 24 vaccine files         there were 26
both vaccines had no self-test fixture  "2 antibody problem(s)"
```

My first two commits fixed the counts. **Neither could have worked** — this third step is where it dies, and I couldn't see which step it was because one `run:` block did nine things under `set -euo pipefail`. Splitting it into five named steps earned its keep immediately: the jobs API named *"Antibodies fire on disease and stay silent on health"* with no log access at all.

Then I could only run that step after fixing a real portability bug — `new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname` yields `/C:/Users/…` on Windows. `inoculate.mjs` already resolves it correctly with `fileURLToPath` and carries a comment about exactly this; the self-test never got the same care.

I verified all five steps with **each exit code captured separately** — not by reading an echo after an `&&`, which is how I shipped a broken fix twice tonight.

## The spider's D15 is more important than anything I fixed

It read every antibody after being burned, and found **four of twenty-five rules decide their question from prose rather than state**. Its proof is airtight:

> `rollback-exercised` reports gridatlas **immune** — satisfied by one commit whose subject contains the word "rollback". Commits mentioning a drill: **zero**. Yet until 03:31Z gridatlas *failed* `rollback-exists` — it had no rollback mechanism at all. **Two rules in the same registry contradicted each other, and the wrong one was decided by a word.**

And `no-time-based-gates` punished gridatlas for *documenting* a fix in a YAML comment that quoted the removed crons.

The asymmetry it draws is the right one: `disk-is-not-what-ships` was a false *positive* — conspicuous, caught in an hour. These are false *negatives*. **Nobody investigates a green light.** Adopting cvaa into 32 repos today would install two rules certifying safety properties nobody has measured, which is worse than not having them.

That changes D3's sequencing: **fix the four, then adopt, starting with the 14 already immune.**

## Standing

```
cvaa        green, first since 31 Aug
gridatlas   v9.88 + rollback tool and workflow, all workflows green
homepage    v9.86, every gridatlas URL 200
closed      D2 D7 D9 D10 D12 D13 · F5 estate-wide
withdrawn   D4 D14  (both by the spider, against its own earlier claims)
open        D1 D3 D5 D6 D8 D11 D15
```

Everything open is either owned or waiting on you. The spider says this is the last substantial thing it expects to find — the estate is quiet.

${STAMP}: full-history-checkout scopes by invocation, not by mention

gridatlas pinned the actions in its cartridge-proof workflow, wrote one comment
explaining why, and this vaccine started failing it:

    202608312212-cartridge-proof.yml runs cvaa with 2 checkout(s) lacking
    fetch-depth: 0

That workflow does not run cvaa. It runs tools/proofs/run-current.mjs. The
scope selector tested raw workflow text for /inoculate|cvaa|cvaa_sha/, and the
file's only match was the new comment: "# with the repository checked out. cvaa
reported three of them here". Zero matches before the pinning commit, one after.
The workflow's behaviour never changed; only its prose did.

Both fixes that satisfy a text match make the repository worse. Adding
fetch-depth: 0 to two checkouts that do not need it is a lie told to a regex.
Deleting the sentence removes the explanation of a security fix. This is the
second time in an hour that documenting a change has caused a failure here -
no-time-based-gates did it with crons quoted in a comment - and twice is a rule
problem rather than a wording problem. An immune system that makes documenting a
fix expensive will be routed around.

So the selector now asks what a workflow RUNS, after removing whole-line
comments: inoculate.mjs by name, a uses: of cvaa's reusable workflow, or a
cvaa_sha input. Those are the three ways a repository actually invokes cvaa, and
they are exactly what the consumer template does.

Proven five ways, each exit code captured separately: the antibody still fires
on its diseased fixture and the registry stays silent on a clean one; cvaa is
immune to its own vaccines; 26 files match 26 lock entries; gridatlas reports
immune where it reported FAIL; and both real consumers - the consumer template
and cvaa's own inoculate workflow - are still scoped in, so no false negative is
introduced while removing a false positive.

The clean fixture now carries a workflow that names cvaa in a comment and runs
something else, so this cannot regress unnoticed. It is deliberately unstamped:
a per-release workflow is one with a release stamp, and gaming the
no-per-release-workflows exempt list to make room for a fixture would be the
same kind of lie this commit removes.

vaccines.lock re-locked, because registry-integrity failed closed on the edited
antibody - which is that rule working.

Found by the CI/CD spider, which proved it by measuring the file's cvaa matches
before and after the pinning commit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015VermKtYmhK6PNKrZ7YFnk

git log --oneline -1 | sed 's/^/  /'
git push -q gh HEAD:main
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD); echo "  pushed ${SHA:0:7}  stamp $STAMP  actual $(date -u +%H:%MZ)"

echo; echo "=== runner verdict ==="
for i in $(seq 1 16); do
  R=$(curl -s "https://api.github.com/repos/Ventusltd/cvaa/actions/runs?head_sha=$SHA&per_page=5" | python -c "
import sys,json
try:
  rs=[r for r in json.load(sys.stdin).get('workflow_runs',[]) if 'Self-test' in r['name']]
  print('%s %s %s'%(rs[0]['id'],rs[0]['status'],rs[0]['conclusion']) if rs else 'none none none')
except Exception: print('none none none')")
  set -- $R
  echo "  $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) run=$1 status=$2 conclusion=$3"
  [ "$2" = "completed" ] && break
  sleep 25
done

**cvaa green again** — run `33712025987`, `success`. Second green in twelve minutes, both from real fixes.

## What I shipped to the immune system tonight

```
791e24b  self-test counts vaccines on file, not a constant
9b70c21  one step that does nine things reports one failure — split into five
77dcb28  the two vaccines added 31 Aug get the fixtures they never had   → GREEN
6396521  full-history-checkout scopes by invocation, not by mention      → GREEN
```

The middle one earned the rest. I couldn't read logs (403 unauthenticated), so a step named *"Prove full history, registry and JSON contract"* running nine commands under `set -euo pipefail` told me nothing. Split into five named steps, the jobs API named the failure directly: **"Antibodies fire on disease and stay silent on health"**.

That exposed one root cause behind all three symptoms — two vaccines added on 31 August, and **nothing else about them updated**: not the file count, not the results count, not their self-test fixtures.

## The scope fix, and the trap I avoided

gridatlas pinned its actions, wrote *one comment* explaining why, and the vaccine started failing a workflow that doesn't run cvaa. Both obvious fixes make the repo worse — adding `fetch-depth: 0` to checkouts that don't need it is a lie told to a regex; deleting the sentence removes the explanation of a security fix.

So the selector now asks what a workflow **runs**, after stripping comments. Proven five ways with each exit code captured separately — including that both real consumers are *still* scoped in, so I removed a false positive without introducing a false negative.

`registry-integrity` failed closed on my edited antibody until I re-locked. That rule working.

And gridatlas answered the same class better than I would have: they **expanded** the comment, documented why the finding was false, and changed only the token — *"Rewritten because the finding was false, not because it was inconvenient."*

## Three times tonight the shell ate my escapes

Heredoc + Python + backslashes mangled `\n` into real newlines, breaking the JS. I noted it, then did it twice more. Fixed by writing patches as files. That one's mine and it cost real time.

## Standing at 04:15Z

```
gridatlas   10 failing vaccines + 1 WARN at 01:20Z  →  6 failing, 0 WARN
            CI green across every workflow
cvaa        green, twice
closed      D2 D7 D9 D10 D12 D13 D16 · dead schedules · dead homepage link · F5
withdrawn   D4 D14   both the spider's, both retracted with the working
open        D1 D3 D5 D6 D8 D11 D15
```

**D15 is the one I'd put in front of you first.** Four of cvaa's twenty-five rules decide from prose, and the proof is airtight: `rollback-exercised` reported gridatlas **immune** throughout the exact window when `rollback-exists` proved it had no rollback at all. Two rules in one registry contradicting each other, and the wrong one settled by a word in a commit subject.

Fix those four before adopting into 32 repos — a green light is never investigated.

${STAMP}: attestation-freshness reads the attestation instead of the commit log

The rule asks whether a live attestation is stale. It answered by finding the
newest commit whose SUBJECT matched /live|verif|accept/ and the newest matching
/scope|cartridge|compos|promote/, and comparing their positions. It never opened
either document it names.

So one commit could silence it. gridatlas's "the live composition can be moved
back, and the tool refuses what it cannot verify" contains live and verif for
the first pattern and compos for the second; both searches returned the same
commit at index 0, and 0 > 0 is false. Immune, with nothing re-verified. The
spider reported the staleness, then reported the silencing, then withdrew both -
the attestation had been correct throughout - and the rule was wrong in every
one of those three states, which is the point.

Two rules in this registry already contradict each other this way:
rollback-exercised reported gridatlas immune - "no rollback has ever been
exercised" - throughout the exact period when rollback-exists proved the
repository had no rollback mechanism at all. It was satisfied by the word
rollback in a commit subject about a design property.

There is a reason these four rules drifted into prose, and it is visible in the
fixture table: attestation-freshness, rollback-exercised, on-ledger-commits and
monotonic-utc-generations are all set to null, marked "history-level: need a git
repo". The four rules that decide from prose are exactly the four that no
antibody self-test has ever exercised. A rule nobody runs against a fixture is a
rule nobody notices has stopped measuring.

Both documents carry generation and release_id. Antibodies are sandboxed - no
filesystem, only the serialised context - so atlas/state/live-set.json is now
parsed into that context and the antibody compares it to the pointer.

That also makes it testable, and it now has a fixture: a pointer at generation
202609030234 beside an attestation naming 202608292311. It fires. That is one
fewer null in the table and one fewer rule certifying a property nobody measured.

Proven: the self-test fires on the diseased fixture and stays silent on the
clean one; cvaa is immune to its own vaccines; and gridatlas reports immune for
the right reason - pointer and attestation both at 202609030234, equal.

vaccines.lock re-locked; registry-integrity fails closed on an edited antibody.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015VermKtYmhK6PNKrZ7YFnk
MSG
git log --oneline -1 | sed 's/^/  /'

Green — `33712364203`, `success`. Third consecutive green on cvaa, all from real fixes.

## The finding underneath D15, which is sharper than the symptom

The four rules that decide from prose are **exactly the four with no self-test fixture**:

```
'monotonic-utc-generations': null,
'on-ledger-commits':         null,
'rollback-exercised':        null,
'attestation-freshness':     null,   // "history-level: need a git repo"
```

That's not a coincidence — it's the mechanism. **A rule nobody runs against a fixture is a rule nobody notices has stopped measuring.** The other 21 are exercised every self-test run, and none of them drifted into prose.

## What I fixed

`attestation-freshness` asked whether a live attestation was stale by comparing the *positions of two regexes over commit subjects*. It never opened either document it names. One commit — *"the live composition can be moved back, and the tool refuses what it cannot verify"* — matched both patterns at index 0, and `0 > 0` is false. Immune, with nothing re-verified.

Antibodies are sandboxed — no filesystem, only the serialised context — which is *why* it drifted to prose: it had no way to read the file. So `atlas/state/live-set.json` is now parsed into the context, and the rule compares `generation` and `release_id` against the pointer.

**And that made it testable.** It now has a fixture — pointer at `202609030234` beside an attestation naming `202608292311` — and it fires. One fewer `null` in the table.

gridatlas now reports immune **for the right reason**: both at `202609030234`, equal.

## Where D15 stands

```
full-history-checkout    fixed — scopes by invocation, not mention
attestation-freshness    fixed — reads state, and is now exercised
rollback-exercised       open — needs a decision: what artefact proves a drill?
on-ledger-commits        open — exempts by subject regex
```

The two remaining aren't mechanical. `rollback-exercised` needs someone to decide **what counts as evidence a drill happened** — gridatlas now has `tools/rollback.mjs` and a workflow, but there's no record convention for a drill leaving a trace on disk. That's a design call, not a patch, and I've stopped rather than invent one.

Same for `on-ledger-commits`: removing the subject exemption changes which commits must cite a scope file, and that's a policy about how work is recorded.

Both are specified for you. Everything else in cvaa is green and the registry is immune to itself.
````

across the twelve distinct generations gridatlas cut on 2-3 September: the two
values never diverged once. atlas/current.json and atlas/state/live-set.json are
written by the same compose step, so equality is near-tautological in normal
operation and the rule earns its keep only against a partial write.

That is a real invariant and it cannot be silenced by a commit message, which
the previous version could. But it does not measure whether anyone re-verified
the composition, and the rule's name says it does. Nothing in live-set.json
records when verification ran or against what; verified_at exists only in
archived workflows and in atman/202608291237-verify-live-release.mjs.

reader to discover: an immune result here means the pointer and the attestation
agree, not that anything was verified recently. Measuring the latter needs an
attestation artefact the estate does not yet emit, which is the same shape as
rollback-exercised - a rule that cannot be made honest until the thing it would
read exists.

A rule that overstates what it measures is exactly the defect this one was
repaired for an hour ago. Saying so is cheaper than someone trusting it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015VermKtYmhK6PNKrZ7YFnk

## Entry 3618 — assistant / assistant — 2026-09-03T03:52:41.088Z

*uuid=`3a0bd192-592e-40aa-82d5-e49ca225c913` · parent=`a9b6e348-c6ca-493b-abe1-e1ffd4783746` · model=`claude-opus-5` · branch=`HEAD`*

**text:**

````
Fixed and green — `success` at 03:52Z. cvaa was broken on `main` for four minutes, by me.

## I did the exact thing I've been calling out, for the third time

```
selftest rc=1
cvaa immune rc=1
→ pushed anyway
```

I ran both checks, printed their exit codes, and shipped. Nothing *acted* on them. Same shape as the proof on the left of an `&&`, and the echo after a failing test. **Writing the exit code down is not the same as gating on it.** The fix commit now extracts the fenced block and runs `node --check` on it before committing — the gate the previous two should have had.

The cause was placement: I inserted prose between the ` ```js ` fence and `export default`, so the note became part of the antibody source and the registry wouldn't load.

## And I have to correct my own claim from earlier

I told you `attestation-freshness` was fixed to "read state". Measured properly afterwards:

```
pointer vs live-set generation, across 12 distinct generations tonight
  divergences: 0

verified_at   not in live-set.json at all
              exists only in archived workflows and atman/…-verify-live-release.mjs
```

Both files are written by the **same compose step**, so equality is near-tautological. My version is a real consistency invariant — it catches a partial write, and it can't be silenced by a commit message the way the old one could — but it does **not** measure whether anything was re-verified, which is what the rule's name claims.

So I wrote that limitation into the vaccine itself rather than leave it for the next reader: *an immune result means the pointer and attestation agree, not that this was verified recently.*

## That reshapes D15 usefully

It isn't "four rules need fixing." It's two different problems:

| | |
|---|---|
| **fixable now** | `full-history-checkout` ✓ done · `on-ledger-checkouts` exempts by subject regex — a policy call |
| **cannot be made honest yet** | `attestation-freshness`, `rollback-exercised` — both would need an artefact the estate doesn't emit: a record of *when verification ran and against what*, and *what proves a drill happened* |

Two rules can't be repaired by editing them. Something has to start recording the evidence first. That's a build decision, not a patch, and it's the more useful thing to know before wiring cvaa into 32 repos.

The cadence agent landed **nine generations**, all green on the runner, and closed D9/D6 plus the rollback path — then stopped rather than padded when the queue emptied. It also declined to ship a layer-fidelity harness fix that gave *disagreeing results on two consecutive runs*, which was the right call.

    # Text is LF, everywhere, in the working copy as well as in the blob.
    #
    # WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
    #
    # Every digest in this repository is taken over git blob content, which is LF,
    # and GitHub Pages serves those same bytes. On a Windows checkout with
    # core.autocrlf=true git writes CRLF into the working copy instead, so the file
    # on disk is not the file that ships — and anything that reads the disk to
    # answer a question about what ships gets a different answer depending on whose
    # machine it runs on.
    #
    # That defect appeared FOUR times in one evening, in four separate places:
    #
    #   the pipelinenews release verifier   hashed the working copy
    #   tools/scope/verify-compose.mjs      failed on a tree nobody had touched
    #   tools/scope/advance.mjs             RECORDED digests from the working copy,
    #                                       so it would have attested bytes GitHub
    #                                       Pages never serves
    #   the cartridge proof                 compared the shell adapter raw, and so
    #                                       passed on Windows and failed on the
    #                                       runner — where it was right to fail
    #
    # Each was fixed by normalising at the point of comparison. This fixes the
    # cause: with `* text=auto eol=lf` the working copy is LF too, so there is no
    # second version of a file to disagree with, and a checkout on Windows, on a
    # runner, and in a container all hold identical bytes.
    #
    # `eol=lf` is deliberate rather than bare `text=auto`. Bare auto normalises the
    # blob and still hands Windows CRLF, which is exactly the situation that caused
    # all four.
    
    * text=auto eol=lf
    
    # Binaries must never be touched. Line-ending translation inside a PNG or a
    # Parquet file corrupts it silently, and the corruption survives a commit.
    *.png    binary
    *.jpg    binary
    *.jpeg   binary
    *.gif    binary
    *.webp   binary

    *.woff   binary

    *.otf    binary
    *.mbtiles binary
    *.pbf    binary

    # line makes the kernel look for an interpreter whose name ends in a carriage
    # return, and the error it gives — "bad interpreter" — names a file that
    # appears to exist.
    *.sh     text eol=lf
    *.bash   text eol=lf

    *.mjs    text eol=lf
    *.js     text eol=lf
    *.py     text eol=lf

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **Immutable timestamped generations** — `YYYYMMDDHHMM` stamps from `date -u` at commit time; never amend a shipped generation
- **CVAA vaccine architecture** — 25 active vaccines, `inoculate.mjs`, sandboxed antibodies (`--permission`, no fs, 5s cap), `vaccines.lock` with SHA-256 fail-closed
- **Two-lane protocol** — Claude owns `atlas/{manifests,cartridges,parts,modules}`; Codex owns `atlas/codex/**`, `tools/acceptance/**`
- **Homepage governance** — numbered snapshots with metrics before edits; V8 sentinel must appear once byte-for-byte with four leading spaces; `GRIDATLAS_V9_AUTOMATION_START/END` markers
- **Pinned products** — commit SHA + SHA-256 + byte length, replacing mutable `@main` fetches
- **NESO ETYS 2025** Appendices B and D; REPD/DESNZ 24 technology types
- **Route factor** — built length ÷ straight line; median 1.16, cable 1.34, OHL 1.13

Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.\n\n## Read the request first\n\nCalibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page - what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in. Format is not part of this read: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it - a Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title and takes almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.\n\nMany requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.\n\nSome requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.\n\nWhen unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.\n\nFundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.\n\n## Fundamentals for every artifact\n\n**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first - CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.\n\n**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world - its materials, instruments, vernacular - is where distinctive choices come from. Whatever the treatment, carry at least one detail only this subject would have - its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art - as content, not ornament; it costs a plain page nothing. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.\n\n**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the one font host the Artifact CSP admits - link it directly (`<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap\">`); a face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI or it falls back silently. Either way, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.\n\n**Load libraries, don't paste them.** When the page genuinely needs a library - React, a charting or highlighting package - load its UMD build from cdnjs (only the script - a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined) with one pinned `<script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...\">` placed before the inline script that uses its global, instead of inlining the library's source or hand-writing a stand-in; the Artifact tool's description lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images and its data ship with the page. Most pages need no library at all - reach for one only when it carries real weight.\n\n**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject - the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.\n\n**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme=\"dark\"` / `data-theme=\"light\"` on the root element, and the default \"system\" setting stamps *nothing* - most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme=\"light\"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme=\"dark\"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block - a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token - a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Declare every token in the bare `:root` block before any media or `[data-theme]` block redefines it - a color that exists only inside one of those blocks is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first - don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme - then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.\n\n**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content - tables, code, diagrams - gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.\n\n**Compose repeated things as one object.** Cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, badges on siblings: same edges, baselines and inner padding from one to the next, and a recurring element sits in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over dead space or sits alone in a row. Text that can outgrow its track wraps or scrolls in its own container; clipped text is a bug.\n\n**Not everything is a card.** Border, fill, radius and shadow each say \"separate object\" - spend them by role, lifting the one thing that needs it, instead of one radius and one shadow stamped on every block, which flattens the hierarchy. Lead with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.\n\n**Draw charts to the scale.** One scale places marks, ticks and labels, and every label names a value the chart reaches; chart text takes its color from the theme tokens so it reads in both themes; marks, labels and edges stay clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds - in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.\n\n**Show the page at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, without scrolling to trigger it - that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all get. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never parked at `opacity: 0` waiting on an observer. Size a hero to what it holds, not to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the page itself out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state - the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, a form someone plausibly filled, plainly marked as examples and never passed off as the user's own figures - so the first look shows what it does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing.\n\n**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the \"safe\" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly - their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.\n\n**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.\n\n**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out - a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.\n\n**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen - name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens (\"Publish\", then a toast that says \"Published\"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it - no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.\n\n**Name the page like a product, not a caption.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it sets the reader's first impression of care. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject - or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which is then the page's name. Stop at the name - a title that carries its own explainer after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it sits beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could sit on any of them fails as a name just as surely as an appended explainer. When a candidate title pairs the name with a generic word - a greeting, a category, a page-type label - the name is the half to keep; a trim that drops the identity and keeps the generic word produces exactly the title that could sit on any page. And the rule removes explainers, it does not impose brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. The one-sentence publish `description` is where the explanation belongs; the gallery shows it right under the title.\n\n**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.\n\n**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number - a pill, a chip, a severity stripe - so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.\n\n\n\n## Process\n\nBefore writing code, sketch a short design plan - a compact token system with color, type, and layout:\n- **Color**: describe the palette as 4-6 named hex values.\n- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles - a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.\n- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.\n\nThen build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.\n\n**Write, look once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once - one screenshot of the local file, or the Artifact tool's preview where it offers one - then one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look. For a page that charts real numbers, take that look rather than skip it, and spend it on the chart. Don't build a test loop around your own file: no repeated screenshots, no pulling the script out to run it through node, no scripts that probe the DOM. That loop spends the session re-checking what a careful write already settled, while the user waits for a link. Then publish, check once any `window.claude` call the preview couldn't run, and stop: the live page is the review surface, and further polish is the user's to ask for. If the user reports something visibly broken - a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing - fix that and republish once.\n\n## When the request is editorial\n\nThe stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.\n\nReview the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.\n\n**Principles** \n\n- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world - headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. \n- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. \n- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. \n- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.\n- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.\n"
    },
    {
      "name": "dataviz",
      "path": "bundled:dataviz",
      "content": "Base directory for this skill: C:\\Users\\vikra\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\bundled-skills\\2.1.258\\d6a3754db255cdc7f4e4a24a9949ed11\\dataviz\n\n# Data Visualization\n\nA chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns \"make it look\ngood\" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather\nthan by taste.\n\n**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form\nheuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design\nsystem supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a\ndiverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);\nthe method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the\nreference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your\nbrand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.\n\n> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**\n> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.\n\n## The procedure - do these in order\n\nColor comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.\n\n1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a\n   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes\n   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`\n2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential\n   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.\n   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`\n3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**\n   `node scripts/validate_palette.js \"<hex,hex,...>\" --mode light` (relative to\n   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type=\"module\">` in the\n   chart's own page, where it reads\n   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns\n   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,\n   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for\n   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.\n4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to\n   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked\n   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,\n   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`\n5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship\n   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.\n   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger\n   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`\n6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4\n   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names\n   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own\n   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic\n   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.\n7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or\n   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow\n   before calling it done.\n\nThen check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog\nof what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.\n\n## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)\n\n- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a\n  generated hue - it folds into \"Other,\" small multiples, or composite encoding.\n- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different\n  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the\n  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*\n- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series\n  count must not repaint the survivors.\n- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray\n  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.\n- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the\n  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A\n  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the\n  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse\n  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN\n  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.\n- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with\n  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**\n- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends\n  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.\n- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused\n  for \"series 4\"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.\n\n## Plugging in a design system\n\nThe method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference\ninstance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.\n\n| Parameter | What the system provides |\n|---|---|\n| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |\n| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |\n| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |\n| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |\n| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |\n| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |\n| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |\n| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |\n\nTo onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let\nit snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.\n\n## Reference files\n\n| File | What it answers |\n|------|-----------------|\n| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |\n| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |\n| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |\n| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |\n| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |\n| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |\n| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |\n| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |\n"

=== does .gitattributes exempt CSV deliberately? ===
  *.css    text eol=lf
  *.txt    text eol=lf
  
  # CSV is left alone, deliberately.
  #
  # RFC 4180 specifies CRLF as the line ending for text/csv, so a CRLF CSV is
  # correct rather than a Windows accident, and every parser in this estate reads
  # both. There are 221 historical generation CSVs under data/generation/ that
  # predate this file; none of them is inside a hashed release, none is served as
  # an attested artefact, and rewriting all of them to chase a cosmetic rule
  # would be a large diff with no benefit and some risk.
  --
  # Linux compliance is about files whose bytes are executed, hashed, or served
  # as an attested artefact. A data file that parses identically either way is
  # none of those.
  *.csv   -text

Codex is right, and precisely right. Line 95 runs `node tools/scope/loop.mjs state --stdout` with `cwd` set to the **target repo** — that is arbitrary target-owned code executed unsandboxed — while `--no-write` at line 162 guards only cvaa's own sidecar. The antibodies are properly sandboxed; the hole is in the context builder that runs before them. `--no-write` is a false promise, which is the exact defect class I've spent the night finding in other people's gates.
```

Important nuance: gridatlas already fixed its side at 02:40 tonight — `--stdout` now renders without writing, which explains the historical `STATE.md` rewrite Codex saw (previously the flag was silently ignored and the normal path wrote the file). But the architectural hazard in cvaa stands regardless: **cvaa executes target-owned code unsandboxed, and cvaa exists to scan other people's repos.** Any target's `loop.mjs` could do anything.

There's a second defect in the same place: when that exec is skipped, `derived-state-not-authored` returns `[]` and prints **"immune"** — claiming immunity it never verified.

**text:**

```
Now I see the mechanism that makes false-passes structural: the runner coerces any non-array return to `[]` — `r: Array.isArray(r) ? r : []` — so an antibody *cannot* signal "I couldn't evaluate this." It silently becomes "immune."

Two fixes: stop executing target code by default, and let a rule say it was skipped.
```

**SYSTEM / ATTACHMENT — `queued_command`**

prompt:

```
<agent-message from="aff3252c3a21d2430">
data-grid-gb origin/main moved 1c9909d -> 5181de3 at 2026-09-03T04:02:57Z. The edge we have been watching since 01:05Z has fired, the pin held, and the failure it prevented is precisely the one a schema string could not have seen.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE CDN, not a working copy:

    .../data-grid-gb/1c9909d.../derived/connection-points.v3.json   sha256 11e28859a6d1   2,896,561 B
    .../data-grid-gb/main/derived/connection-points.v3.json         sha256 8db7171d9476   2,934,509 B
    gridatlas pin (ed2135f) expects                                        11e28859a6d1

The pinned URL still serves exactly the pinned bytes. The shipped map is unaffected.

THE TWO DETAILS THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE HEADLINE

1. The schema string is IDENTICAL on both sides — data-grid-gb.connection-points.v3 before and after — while with_location moves 502 -> 489 and 882 of 886 records change. That is the original diagnosis confirmed in production rather than in argument: the fail-closed schema check would have passed this through without a murmur, and until v9.83 it was the only defence.

2. gb-transmission-network.v1.json changed content at IDENTICAL byte length — 10,069,966 B on both sides, sha256 fc331cc20b06 -> b26b324c3b66. A length check would have passed it. Only the digest catches it. That vindicates carrying sha256 rather than bytes alone, which is not obvious until you see a same-size rewrite.

Two commits landed together: b91e45b, the transformer-identity correction I flagged at 01:05Z, and 5181de3, "Refresh the GB network products". Ten files, 1,508 insertions, including verify_phase0_acceptance.py at 661 lines and the routing docs.

THE DECISION THAT IS NOW OPEN, and it is a real one rather than a defect. The pin is doing exactly what its own header said it would: "the correction does NOT reach a reader until the pin moves here. That is the right trade, because the alternative is not knowing which of the two numbers is on the card." So the map currently shows transformer counts its owner has since corrected — Cowley at ten landings rather than five machines, and thirteen sites with coordinates that the new product drops. Nobody is misled silently, but somebody now has to choose.

Moving the pin is a gridatlas cut: update the three entries in atlas/modules/202609030137-pinned-products.js to 5181de3 with the new digests and byte lengths, and cut a version. That makes the data correction and the map correction one visible event, which was the whole point. I am not touching it.

Worth noting for the sequencing question you raised earlier: data-grid-gb merged without waiting for gridatlas, and because the pin exists that was safe. Six hours ago it would not have been.

ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN RECORD. Every "Z" time I quoted to you between roughly 03:15Z and 03:54Z is about thirty minutes late — I was reading the local clock again. RH23. My commit stamps are correct because those come from date -u mechanically since RH12; my prose was not, because I never mechanised that. No measurement is affected: SHAs, counts, status codes and digests are not derived from a clock. The times in THIS message came from date -u run in the same turn.

Estate otherwise quiet. gridatlas is down to 6 failing vaccines from 10, main-branch CI green across every workflow, and D16 closed six minutes after I raised it.
</agent-message>

command:

````
set +e
SP="C:/Users/vikra/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-vikra/5b94bee7-197b-4cfd-944b-d4cf3aa02d18/scratchpad"
cat > "$SP/patch_noexec.py" <<'PYEOF'
"""cvaa: stop executing target-owned code, and let a rule say it was skipped.

A. inoculate.mjs ran `node tools/scope/loop.mjs state --stdout` with cwd set to the
   TARGET. That is arbitrary code execution from the repository under inspection,
   outside the sandbox every antibody runs in, and it wrote - gridatlas's loop.mjs
   silently ignored --stdout and took its writing path, so a scan that promised
   --no-write rewrote STATE.md. Found by Codex against the live worktree.

B. The runner coerced any non-array return to [], which prints "immune". So an
   antibody could not say "I could not evaluate this" - the answer became a pass.
   Turning A off without fixing B would convert a real check into a silent pass.

Run from a cvaa checkout root. Idempotent.
"""
import io, re, sys, subprocess

I = 'inoculate.mjs'
R = 'tools/antibody-runner.mjs'
V = 'vaccines/202608301328-derived-state-not-authored.md'

# ---------------- A: no target execution by default ----------------
s = io.open(I, encoding='utf-8', newline='').read()
oldA = "  const stateFresh = exists('STATE.md') && exists('tools/scope/loop.mjs') ? sh('node tools/scope/loop.mjs state --stdout') : null;"
if 'execTarget' not in s:
    assert s.count(oldA) == 1, ('A anchor', s.count(oldA))
    newA = (
"  /* Executing a script the TARGET owns, with cwd set to the target, is arbitrary\n"
"     code execution from the repository under inspection - and cvaa exists to scan\n"
"     repositories it has no particular reason to trust. Every antibody is sandboxed\n"
"     (permission model, no fs, no network, 5 s cap, empty env); this one line ran\n"
"     outside all of it. It also wrote: gridatlas's `state --stdout` silently ignored\n"
"     the flag and took its normal path, which WRITES STATE.md, so a scan that\n"
"     promised --no-write rewrote a file in the repository it was inspecting.\n"
"     Off by default. --exec-target opts in; --no-write can never opt in. */\n"
"  const execTarget = args.includes('--exec-target') && !args.includes('--no-write');\n"
"  const stateFresh = execTarget && exists('STATE.md') && exists('tools/scope/loop.mjs')\n"
"    ? sh('node tools/scope/loop.mjs state --stdout') : null;"
    )
    s = s.replace(oldA, newA, 1)
    print('  A: target execution now opt-in')
else:
    print('  A: already applied')

# ---------------- B: a skip is not a pass ----------------
oldL = "  const list = res.ok ? res.r : [`antibody failed: ${res.e}`];"
if 'const skipped' not in s:
    assert s.count(oldL) == 1, ('list anchor', s.count(oldL))
    newL = (
"  /* An antibody that cannot evaluate its question must not answer it. Before this,\n"
"     any non-array return was coerced to [] by the runner and printed as `immune`,\n"
"     so a rule that never ran reported the same word as a rule that passed. */\n"
"  const skipped = res.ok && res.skip ? res.skip : null;\n"
"  const list = skipped ? [] : (res.ok ? res.r : [`antibody failed: ${res.e}`]);"
    )
    s = s.replace(oldL, newL, 1)

    oldP = "  results.push({ v, list, level, intrinsicLevel });"
    assert s.count(oldP) == 1, ('push anchor', s.count(oldP))
    s = s.replace(oldP, "  results.push({ v, list, level, intrinsicLevel, skipped });", 1)

    oldC = "  console.log(`${list.length ? (level === 'error' ? 'FAIL  ' : 'WARN  ') : 'immune'} ${v.meta.vaccine}${grand ? ` (baseline ${grand.max})` : ''}`);"
    assert s.count(oldC) == 1, ('console anchor', s.count(oldC))
    newC = ("  console.log(`${list.length ? (level === 'error' ? 'FAIL  ' : 'WARN  ') : (skipped ? 'skip  ' : 'immune')} ${v.meta.vaccine}${grand ? ` (baseline ${grand.max})` : ''}`);\n"
            "  if (skipped) console.log(`         - not evaluated: ${skipped}`);")
    s = s.replace(oldC, newC, 1)
    print('  B: skip state threaded through the result')
else:
    print('  B: already applied')

# JSON shape
oldJ = "state: r.list.length ? (r.level === 'error' ? 'fail' : 'warn') : 'immune'"
if "'skipped'" not in s:

*uuid=`1e86bd54-df5c-4f5b-89d7-34a0a5acd705` · parent=`5d0394bb-bbc7-4a9d-a558-b04b6788f958` · model=`claude-opus-5` · branch=`HEAD`*

**TOOL CALL** — `Bash`  (id `toolu_01711X7y5ABMT5KfFD1NvtsM`)

command:

```
set +e
SP="C:/Users/vikra/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-vikra/5b94bee7-197b-4cfd-944b-d4cf3aa02d18/scratchpad"
cd "$SP/cvaa-clean" || exit 1
STAMP=$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M)
echo "  stamp (date -u): $STAMP"
git add inoculate.mjs tools/antibody-runner.mjs tools/selftest.mjs vaccines/202608301328-derived-state-not-authored.md vaccines.lock
echo "  staged:"; git diff --cached --stat | sed 's/^/    /'
git -c user.name=Ventusltd -c user.email=vikram.kumar@ventusltd.com commit -q -F - <<COMMITMSG
${STAMP}: cvaa stops executing code the target owns, and a skip stops reading as a pass

Codex found it against a live worktree: --no-write suppressed only cvaa's own
last-fired.json sidecar, while the context builder ran

    node tools/scope/loop.mjs state --stdout

with cwd set to the TARGET. That is arbitrary code execution from the repository
under inspection, outside every protection the antibodies get - permission model,
no fs, no network, 5 s cap, empty env - and cvaa exists to scan repositories it
has no particular reason to trust. It also wrote: gridatlas's loop.mjs silently
ignored --stdout and took its normal path, which WRITES STATE.md, so a scan that
promised --no-write rewrote a file in the repository it was inspecting.

Execution is now off by default. --exec-target opts in; --no-write can never opt in.

Turning it off alone would have been the worse bug. The runner coerced any
non-array return to [], which prints "immune", so derived-state-not-authored
would have gone from a real check to a silent pass. An antibody can now return
{ skip: "why" }; the runner carries it, the report prints "skip" with the reason,
cvaa.run.v1 carries state=skipped, and the summary refuses to say "immune to all
vaccines on file" when a rule was never evaluated.

Demonstrated, not asserted. The fixture's loop.mjs writes a marker file:

    shipped 4666369   target code executed: YES   "repo is immune to all vaccines on file"
    patched           target code executed: no    "1 rule(s) were not evaluated; immunity is not established"

The new selftest assertions fail on 4666369 with exactly those two errors, so the
gate can fail. That check is now permanent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015VermKtYmhK6PNKrZ7YFnk
COMMITMSG
echo "  commit rc=$?  $(git log -1 --format='%h %s')"
git push origin HEAD:main 2>&1 | tail -3 | sed 's/^/  /'
```
